canDos.textEn: Can exchange greetings with a person you are meeting for the first time in a long time.
Can talk in simple terms about how you have been recently when asked by a close person.
Can talk in simple terms about your work in Japan.
Can talk in simple terms about your hobbies and favorite things to do.
Can ask and answer questions about how you spend your days off.
Can read staff descriptions posted in a store, facility, etc. and understand their families, hobbies, etc.
Can write in simple terms about your hobbies, your days off, etc. for staff descriptions posted at work.
Can watch a short video about the four seasons in Japan and understand seasonal characteristics.
Can talk in simple terms about the seasonal characteristics of your own country.
Can talk in simple terms about your favorite season and the reason.
Can exchange greetings while talking about the weather.
Can listen to the weather forecast and mostly understand it.
Can read and understand simple posts about the weather on social media.
Can talk in simple terms about your impressions of your town.
Can ask questions about recommended places around town and understand the answers.
Can look at a town map and get information about famous spots, stores, etc.
Can ask and understand directions.
Can ask and understand directions on the phone.
Can give directions to the destination by car when, for example, someone gives you a ride.
Can ask and understand the time and place to meet.
Can talk about and decide the time and place to meet.
Can read and understand a message saying that the person you are meeting will be late.
Can write a message saying that you will be late for the arranged time.
Can ask someone out to eat, go shopping, or go to an event while asking about their experience and interest.
Can discuss what to do next and where to go while you are out with someone.
Can give your impressions about the event to the person you went with.
Can talk in simple terms about your experience learning Japanese.
Can give your impressions and comments about learning Japanese.
Can ask someone for help when, for example, you have a problem with Japanese.
Can read an online forum about learning Japanese and understand the recommended study methods.
Can find and understand information such as the place, date, and time of lessons offered at a local community center, etc.
Can ask questions about the lesson you are interested in at a local government office and understand the answers.
Can ask friends or answer questions about Japanese-language classes in the community.
Can answer questions about your experience or your goals in learning Japanese, in order to participate in Japanese-language classes.
Can discuss who will bring which item when, for example, having a barbecue.
Can discuss what to buy when, for example, having a house party.
Can ask store staff about the ingredients and expiration dates of food and understand the answers.
Can read food labels to check if the food contains something you cannot eat.
Can give your impressions about the appearance of food.
Can comment about the recommended food after eating it.
Can ask or answer questions about the taste, ingredients, etc. of dishes.
Can read and understand cooking instructions for making instant food.
Can tell your supervisor what is going on when you have a problem at work.
Can briefly answer when asked about the status of work.
Can ask about and understand, for example, how to use a machine at work.
Can listen to and understand explanations and instructions on tasks at work.
Can read and understand a simple email for work.
Can call your workplace to say that you will be late or take the day off.
Can ask for permission from a co-worker when leaving the area for a moment.
Can ask for permission in advance when you want to take a day off from work.
Can ask and understand how to fill out a form, such as a vacation request.
Can explain in simple terms your symptoms at the hospital.
Can listen to and understand the doctor at the hospital.
Can fill out the necessary information on a questionnaire form at the hospital reception desk.
Can listen to instructions about medicine and understand directions for use and precautions.
Can read instructions about medicine and understand directions for use and dosage.
Can give advice when someone is feeling unwell, or listen to and understand the advice.
Can talk about what you are mindful of to maintain your health.
Can look at news about an epidemic illness and more or less understand the contents, such as its name, symptoms, and prevention methods.
Can look at a poster about an illness at a hospital and understand the symptoms, prevention methods, etc.
Can exchange basic greetings when you visit someone’s house.
Can give a simple explanation about a gift you give.
Can talk about your belongings, for example, where you bought it or who gave it to you.
Can write a simple email to thank someone who, for example, invited you to their house.
Can say congratulations for a birthday, wedding, etc.
Can discuss what to give when selecting a gift for someone.
Can thank someone and offer comments when someone gives you a gift.
Can read and understand a post on social media that your friend wrote on their birthday.
Can write a message of congratulations or goodbye on a card.
